perQuestion.answer: Because the backtests showed that frequent narrowing/re-centering lost to a wide passive range. On 720d, narrowing earned about 4× more fees ($2169 vs $541 on cbBTC), but IL and re-centering costs (65 and 88 rebalances) consumed more than the extra fees. perQuestion.answer: Because both legs of cbBTC/WETH are crypto, the pair carries full crypto beta with no stable cushion. Over the 365-day backtest HODL 50/50 fell −51.5% APR with a max drawdown of 61.5%, even though LP-vs-HODL alpha was the best of all pools (+11.42 for adapt k2h24). So the risk lies in exposure, not LP quality. The sleeve was deliberately given a smaller weight (a smaller allocation than the ETH/stable core), since in a falling regime neither leg is stable. By contrast, ETH/stable has a stable leg that acts as a cushion.

perQuestion.answer: The chunks do not say the LP earned less in fees during an uptrend than in flat markets. They explain why LP results were worse in uptrends, which is a different question. A concentrated LP sells into rallies, so in a trending year that costs more than the fees earn. In up windows the strategies lost to HODL, and up windows produced the record losses. Narrowing also earned far more fees but still finished lower. The chunks give no fee comparison between up and flat regimes.
